meta.title: About — Daniel Oliver Racing
meta.description: From sim racing and software engineering to an FIA international licence in six months. The full story — and the road to IMSA 2026.

hero.intro: Racing driver and software engineer. This is how a sim rig and an engineer's mindset became an FIA licence, a Praga campaign, and a 2026 IMSA debut.

sections.title: No family pedigree. A different starting grid.
sections.imageAlt: Daniel Oliver focused in his race suit before a test session at Sebring
body: Most racing drivers are handed a kart before they can spell their own name. I wasn't. There's no family team in my past, no racing dynasty, no childhood trophy shelf.

I came to motorsport as a software engineer who fell in love with sim racing — and refused to accept that the simulator was where the story had to end. What I lacked in pedigree I made up for in method: break the problem down, measure everything, iterate relentlessly.

sections.title: Sim to grid in six months.
sections.imageAlt: Daniel Oliver alongside the #38 Project Limit Break prototype
body: When I decided to make the jump from virtual to real, I treated it like an engineering project with a deadline. Within roughly six months of starting, I'd earned an FIA international racing licence — and taken multiple wins along the way.

The sim gave me racecraft, reference points and thousands of laps of deliberate practice. The real car demanded everything else: physicality, feel, and the discipline to perform when there's no reset button. Bridging that gap, systematically, is the thing I'm most proud of.

sections.title: Every lap is a dataset. Every mistake, an experiment.
sections.imageAlt: The Praga prototype on track at Silverstone
body: I drive the way I build software: hypothesis, test, measure, refine. Telemetry doesn't flatter you and it doesn't lie — it just tells you where the time is. That honesty is the whole game.

Racing a Praga prototype in UK events at circuits like Brands Hatch and Silverstone has been the proving ground for this sim-to-real methodology: experiments run cheaply in the simulator, validated at speed on track.

sections.title: IMSA 2026 — and opening the door behind me.
sections.imageAlt: Project Limit Break build work in progress
body: In 2026 I make my debut in the IMSA VP Racing SportsCar Challenge, racing endurance rounds with a co-driver. It's the biggest test yet of the data-driven approach — longer stints, shared strategy, and races won in the details.

Alongside the racing is Project Limit Break, my initiative through Limit Break Engineering: a student exposure program at IMSA race weekends, where students work directly alongside engineers, strategists, media crews and mechanics — plus sim-to-real coaching for drivers making the same leap I did. The path I took shouldn't be a one-off. It should be a blueprint.
